verdict.rationale: Asana's own docs confirm a native Rules feature: developers can extend it with custom "rule actions" and app components on the surface of rules, AI Studio is billed as "powerful no-code automations", and the PagerDuty integration fires via Rules. However, the evidence never describes how triggers and actions are configured, what triggers exist, or any limits, so the depth of the rule builder is unproven. Third-party tools (Zapier, n8n) and raw webhooks/API earn no credit here. Missing for 10: documentation of the trigger/action rule builder (available triggers, conditions, actions), limits or plan availability, and hands-on or independent corroboration of rules eliminating manual steps.
